description: Use first, whenever someone describes a failure they are seeing. Pass the symptoms as a sentence or a few words, in English or Korean; returns the reviewed public post-incident reports that answer it, best match first: the search ranks every case and keeps only those judged relevant to the sentence, usually a handful, and none when the library has no such incident (`total` 0). `total` is how many, `results` is one page of them in full (each with the case id, the page url and the source link), `matched` is every one as a row, and `next_cursor` fetches the next page. `interpreted` lists the values the sentence named (the search moves cases carrying them up) and any organisation it named (a filter to choose, not a ranking signal); `facets` count the results by root cause, component, symptom, contributing factor and organisation with the case ids, which answers 'what usually caused this' from the same call. The optional slug filters keep only cases carrying those values (AND); take slugs from facets, interpreted or vocab. Follow with get_incident for the full case.

component.description: Keep only cases with this component slug, e.g. coredns

domain.description: Keep only cases in this domain, e.g. kubernetes or ai-infra

factor.description: Keep only cases with this contributing factor slug, e.g. no-alerting

lang.description: ko returns the Korean text of each field where the reviewers wrote one

org.description: Keep only cases of this organisation, by slug, e.g. github (from facets.orgs, interpreted or vocab)

root_cause.description: Keep only cases with this root cause slug, e.g. capacity

symptom.description: Keep only cases with this symptom slug, e.g. pod-pending

symptoms.description: What is observed, as a sentence or a few words, e.g. 'pods cannot get an IP, nodes show no available addresses' or 'coredns oom'. Leave it out to list every case under the slug filters, newest first; then at least one filter is required

name: search_incidents
title: Search incidents by symptoms
